name: finder-tags
title: Finder Tags
description: Tag Finder selections, browse your tags, and find tagged files on your Mac.
author: 0xdhrv

commands.name: tag-selected-files
commands.title: Tag Selected Files
commands.description: Add or remove Finder tags on the selected files

commands.name: quick-tag
commands.title: Quick Tag
commands.description: Apply comma-separated tags to the Finder selection, or start with a minus to remove tags

commands.name: search-tags
commands.title: Search Tags
commands.description: Browse Finder tags with file counts, rename tags, or remove tags across indexed files

commands.name: search-files-by-tag
commands.title: Search Files by Tag
commands.description: Find files with one or more Finder tags, preview files, and manage their tags

tools.name: list-tags
tools.title: List Tags
tools.description: List Finder tags with colours and file counts in configured search folders.

tools.name: find-files-by-tag
tools.title: Find Files by Tag
tools.description: Find up to 50 files by Finder tags, kind, and optional modification date range.

tools.name: tag-files
tools.title: Tag Files
tools.description: Add Finder tags to explicit paths or the current Finder selection after confirmation.

tools.name: untag-files
tools.title: Untag Files
tools.description: Remove specified Finder tags from explicit paths or the current Finder selection after confirmation.

preferences.name: searchScope
preferences.title: Search Scope
preferences.description: An absolute folder path or ~ for your home folder. Counts and tag-wide actions are limited to this scope and extra folders.

preferences.name: extraFolders
preferences.title: Extra Folders
preferences.description: Additional absolute folder paths, separated by semicolons or newlines.

preferences.name: closeAfterTagging
preferences.title: After Tagging
preferences.label: Close Raycast after tagging selected files
preferences.description: Close Raycast after a successful change in Tag Selected Files. Quick Tag always shows a HUD.

preferences.name: sortByCount
preferences.title: Tag Order
preferences.label: Sort tags by file count instead of name
preferences.description: Show the most-used tags first. Turn off to sort alphabetically.

ai.instructions: Finder Tags manages macOS Finder tags locally. Before calling tag-files or untag-files, always call list-tags first and reuse existing tag spelling when names differ only in case. An empty list is not proof that a specific tag does not exist because Spotlight may be delayed or unavailable. Still run an explicitly requested search or create a new tag when needed. For these files, the selection, or no explicit paths, omit paths from tag-files and untag-files; the tools resolve the Finder selection. Never invent paths. Every write tool asks for confirmation listing the exact files and tags. When the user has asked to tag or untag files, call the write tool directly after resolving spelling; do not ask a separate conversational confirmation. A new tag needs no separate creation step or approval. For search-and-tag requests, first call find-files-by-tag and then pass only its returned paths to the write tool. Searches return at most 50 files. If hasMore is true, explain the limit and ask the user to narrow the search before changing everything; never claim all matches were changed. modifiedAfter is inclusive and modifiedBefore is exclusive. For a named month, use both bounds; clarify the year when unclear. Report failures and indexing warnings, and never claim a failed file changed. Tag-wide changes are restricted to indexed files in configured search folders. When list-tags reports countsArePartial, counts are lower bounds; zero means no files could be found, not that a saved tag is unused. Explain the search warning when discussing usage.
